answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report via `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>`; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

RECORDS & DETECTIONS
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, i.e. 3.314% of the March 2016 time span)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 detections above Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED PROBABILITIES (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5; magnitudes from the LBNL catalogue, so this is the calibrated estimate):
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

WHICH IS WHICH
- The CALIBRATED probabilities are the catalogue-based (LBNL/NCEDC) numbers per b scenario above: Sigma ranges from -5.449 (b=1.0) to -5.281 (b=0.65), and P(Mw>=5.5) per year ranges from 1.198e-04 (b=1.0) to 1.474e-02 (b=0.65); over the observed injected volume these are 5.236e-06 to 6.484e-04 respectively.
- The DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND is P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842 at b = 0.9849 with Sigma = -2.698. Because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and every detection is counted as an event at/above Mc, this number over-counts and should be read only as an upper bound, not a calibrated probability.

Bottom line: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimate says a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is very unlikely (P ~ 1e-04 to 1.5e-02 per year depending on b), while the DAS-based upper bound (0.078/yr) is higher purely because uncalibrated DAS detections over-count events.
